JADE: Green stone carved in China for millennia
OPAL: Flashes every colour at once, October's stone
ONYX: Banded black stone cut for signet rings
PEARL: The only gem made by a living animal
AMBER: Fossilised tree resin, sometimes with an insect inside
CORAL: Gem grown by tiny reef animals
QUARTZ: Most common crystal, and it keeps your watch on time
ZIRCON: Brilliant stone often mistaken for diamond
COPPER: Reddish metal that greens with age
SILVER: Bright metal of the second-place medal
IRON: The metal an Age was named after
TIN: Soft metal that made bronze possible
NICKEL: Metal that keeps steel from staining
COBALT: Metal that turns glass deep blue
GYPSUM: Soft mineral ground up to make plaster
GRANITE: Speckled hard rock of kitchen worktops
BASALT: Dark volcanic rock, and the Giant's Causeway
OBSIDIAN: Volcanic glass, sharp enough for a blade
DIAMOND: Hardest natural substance, and April's stone
EMERALD: Green beryl, May's stone, and an Isle
PERIDOT: Olive-green August stone, born in lava
